question: At equal native synthesis budgets, does the native two-mass source family predict held-out vowels, pitch and pressure better or worse than the prescribed geometric glottis, for off-grid synthetic generators from both families?
pipeline: Production singing_physics.phonation: fit_phonation (calibration), forecast_phonation_bank (frozen held-out banks), score_phonation_bank (one extraction per held-out frame, no synthesis). Generators use synthesize_phonation.
frozen_before_run: This file, run.py and test_protocol.py are committed before run.py is executed. No generator shape or generator anatomy was synthesized before that commit.
pilot_disclosure: Before freezing, only grid and app shapes were synthesized: two-mass (XB=XT, EAA, DF) = (.005,0,1), (.01,0,1), (.015,0,1), (.015,.005,1), (.01,0,1.3) and geometric PS -0.2/0/0.2, at 65-600 Hz on vowel a (all five vowels for the app shapes), on the template anatomy and single-parameter changes (hard_palate_length 4.8; lip_width 0.7-1.5); plus geometric PS 0 at 190 Hz for pharynx_length 5.0/6.5, larynx_length 2.5/3.5, lip_width 0.8/1.3 and hard_palate_length 4.8 across a, e, o, u. Those pilots chose the tract options (pharynx and larynx length change e/o harmonic slope; hard_palate_length barely does) and showed that two-mass simulated pitch differs from requested F0 by up to about 20%. No generator shape or generator anatomy below was synthesized before the protocol commit.
candidate_ids: t{tract index}-{family}-{shape index}; 2 tracts x 3 shapes x 2 families = 12 candidates, 6 per family
candidate_f0_rule: A candidate's F0 control for a calibration trial is the pitch the canonical extractor measures in that trial's generator frame, as the app does. JA, PR and gain are the declared trial values. A generator frame without a measured pitch makes that generator unevaluable; it is reported, not replaced.
heldout_rule: Each held-out bank shares the declared controls (F0 190 Hz requested for every alternative and for the generator), uses reference trial cal-a, and freezes all 36 alternatives before the generator's held-out frame is synthesized.
nearest_grid_rule: Scoring-only. Tract: the option nearer in anatomy_fraction. Shape: smallest Euclidean distance within the generator's family after dividing each control by its grid range (PS 0.4; XB 0.01; EAA 0.005; DF 0.3).

scores.primary: score: production mean standardized discrepancy over pitchHz, periodicity, spectralFlatness, harmonicSpectralSlopeDbOctave
scores.pitch_excluded: score_excluding_pitch: the same terms without pitchHz. In the pitch-excluded analysis both selection and held-out comparison use it.

selection: For each generator and family, the selected candidate is the family's joint candidate with the lowest calibration score (ties by candidate_id). A family with no scorable calibration candidate has no selection.
metrics: paired held-out discrepancy: for each (generator, held-out vowel) case, the held-out discrepancy of each family's selected candidate against the same frame, and their difference (two_mass minus geometric)
win: a family wins a case when its selected candidate is scorable and either the other family's is not, or its discrepancy is lower by more than the tie margin

unscorable rate: per family, the fraction of its 6 joint alternatives per case, and the fraction of its selected candidates, that are unscorable at held-out; an unscorable selected candidate is a failure, never a skipped case
true-family rank: position in the held-out joint ranking of the best-ranked alternative from the generator's family (1 is best); null when no alternative of that family is scorable
nearest-grid rank: position of the declared nearest grid candidate in the held-out joint ranking; null when unscorable
F0 mismatch: per family, simulated minus requested F0 over every calibration prediction and bank alternative with a measured pitch
decision_rule: Over the 8 (generator, held-out vowel) cases: positive (two-mass predicts held-out better) if two-mass wins at least 6 cases under both the primary and the pitch-excluded score and has no more failures than geometric; negative if geometric wins at least 6 cases under both scores and has no more failures than two-mass; otherwise inconclusive. An unevaluable generator contributes its cases as failures for both families.
interpretation: Conditional finite-support comparison on synthetic native audio from both families. Generators favour their own family by construction, so a family must also win cases generated by the other family to reach the decision threshold. No anatomical uniqueness, calibrated probability, tissue recovery, vocal-fold contact or human singing claim.
